entries.name: Word Rain
entries.description: Words fall like rain, piling up more and more.

entries.name: Cursor Typing
entries.description: On a black background, a cursor types character by character, typing and then deleting.
entries.fit: things you can't bring yourself to say, inner monologue

entries.name: Big Type Impact
entries.description: Word after word slams into the picture, on the beat.
entries.fit: emotional outbursts, key lines, music video choruses

entries.name: Word Tunnel
entries.description: Words form ring after ring, and the camera burrows inward.
entries.fit: being unable to make sense of something, thoughts spiraling deeper

entries.name: Words Scatter and Reform
entries.description: A sentence scatters into particles and reforms into a different sentence.
entries.fit: a change of heart, a new way of understanding

entries.name: Flowing Threads
entries.description: Countless fine threads flow with an invisible wind.

entries.name: Firefly Dust
entries.description: Warm-colored points of light drift slowly upward, some far, some near.
entries.fit: warmth, memories, finding the light again

entries.name: Particles Forming Shapes
entries.description: Particles gather into a heart, a house, a person, then scatter.
entries.fit: concrete things: home, relationships, a person

entries.name: Starfield Connections
entries.description: Points connect into a web, and the warm one in the middle is you.

entries.name: Breathing Circle
entries.description: A cloud of particles swells and shrinks with the breath.

entries.name: Spreading Ink Wash
entries.description: Ink bleeds outward across rice paper, bloom after bloom.

entries.name: Single-Stroke Drawing
entries.description: A single line slowly draws mountains, a sun, and a small figure.
entries.fit: the outline of a person or an event

entries.name: Inner Contour Lines
entries.description: Like contour lines on a map, constantly rising and falling.
entries.fit: emotional ups and downs, the terrain of the heart

entries.name: Ripples
entries.description: One drop falls, and ring after ring spreads out.
entries.fit: the impact of a single sentence, aftermath

entries.name: Rainy Window
entries.description: Raindrops on glass, with blurred night lights behind.

entries.name: Window Light and Dust
entries.description: A beam of light comes through a window, with dust drifting in the light.

entries.name: Snow and Sparks
entries.description: Snow falls, and a few sparks drift upward.
entries.fit: farewell, endings, a little warmth in the cold

entries.name: Daybreak
entries.description: The sky slowly warms from deep blue, and the sun rises.

entries.name: Minimal Geometry
entries.description: Circles, squares, and semicircles roll, drop, and grow on a solid color.

entries.name: Layered Paper Cut-Outs
entries.description: Layer upon layer of paper pieces with shadows, the front moving fast and the back slow.

entries.name: ASCII Art
entries.description: The whole picture is made of characters, like an old computer screen.

entries.name: Growing Charts
entries.description: Bars grow one by one, numbers tick up, then they connect into a line.

entries.name: Relationship Diagram
entries.description: Arrows between people are drawn one by one, each with the words that were said written on it.

entries.name: Split-Screen Comparison
entries.description: The past on the left, the present on the right, a line in between.
entries.fit: past and present, parents and children

entries.name: Old Film
entries.description: Grain, flicker, scratches, light leaks at the edges.
entries.fit: memories, the old days, a unified material feel across the whole film

entries.name: Signal Glitch
entries.description: The picture slips into misregistration, colors separate, and it suddenly flashes.
entries.fit: breakdown, chaos, words being cut off

entries.name: Hand-Drawn Whiteboard Explainer
entries.description: White background; a hand (or a pen) draws as it explains, with lines drawn first and then colored.
entries.fit: Passages explaining concepts and principles. For example, "the large language model is the brain, the Harness is the hands and feet".

entries.name: Handwritten Paper Notes
entries.description: Cream paper; marker annotations drawn stroke by stroke, handwritten text, big bold headlines, and now and then the whole frame snaps to dark.
entries.fit: Listing points, explaining methods, "here is how you can do it" passages.

entries.name: 3Blue1Brown-Style Explainer
entries.description: Dark background; formulas and shapes morph and derive step by step, explained very clearly.
entries.fit: Science-explainer track: explaining principles and data.

entries.name: Beginner-Friendly Explainer
entries.description: Any art style; what matters is the way of explaining: start from an everyday example and build step by step up to the technical terms.
entries.fit: A whole episode of the science-explainer track, or the "first explain what X is" section of the Feeling track.

entries.name: Timeline and History
entries.description: A timeline moves forward, and each node pops up an event.
entries.fit: "How I got through these three months", "How AI got to where it is today".

entries.name: How It Works Breakdown
entries.description: Take a thing apart and demonstrate step by step how it works inside.
entries.fit: The announcement-scraping example (schedule, fetch, filter, summarize, remind), explaining "how exactly it does that".

entries.name: Recipe-Style Steps
entries.description: Like a cocktail tutorial: start from an empty glass, label the name and amount of each ingredient as it goes in, and end with the finished drink.
entries.fit: Teaching passages like "you only need these few steps to make a small tool".

entries.name: Five-Act Explainer
entries.description: Five scenes tell one story.
entries.fit: The skeleton of a science-explainer episode, or a passage about a tool in the Feeling track.

entries.name: Four-Part Launch Film
entries.description: The big picture, the pain point, the solution, the benefits: four parts, ending with a logo animation.
entries.fit: Passages introducing a new tool or skill.

entries.name: Voiceover with Word-by-Word Captions
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: White background, one typeface; captions type out word by word as the speaker talks, with real images and a slowly drifting camera.
entries.fit: The main thread of the whole film. For a film with someone explaining or doing voiceover, the captions must line up.

entries.name: Emotional Arc: Chaos, Control, Clarity
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: One arc across the whole film. The picture is messy at the start, gradually gets put in order, and ends cleanly on one line. Transitions morph the same shape; no hard cuts.
entries.fit: The structure of a whole episode.

entries.name: Abstract Concept as Visuals
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: No specific people or objects; shapes, text and color changes express a feeling.
entries.fit: Passages about fear, anxiety, unease, or the feeling of "overthinking".

entries.name: Life Cycle Loop
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: The same person from childhood to old age, then seamlessly back to the beginning.
entries.fit: Passages about a long span of time, such as "never stop learning" or "always learning".

entries.name: Paper-Cut Shadow Puppets
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: Paper-cut silhouettes perform behind a light, with soft sound.
entries.fit: Passages about home, memories, warmth. Works well in vertical format.

entries.name: First-Person Hand-Drawn Stop-Motion
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: Hand-drawn stop-motion, a little jittery frame by frame, where the thing on screen speaks for itself.
entries.fit: Letting an object speak for you, for example letting "that little tool that scrapes announcements" introduce itself.

entries.name: Wordless Sound-Driven Short
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: No dialogue; the story is told entirely by picture and sound.
entries.fit: Opening or closing titles, or a short bridge between two sections.

entries.name: Symmetrical Warm Scenic Shots
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: Left-right symmetrical frame in soft warm pinks, like an exquisite little stage. For example, the four seasons flowing past a train window, a cup of coffee on the table.
entries.fit: Passages about time passing or pausing to think, for example "the time the channel was off air".

entries.name: 3D Sunset Sky with One Line
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: A 3D scene with sunset, purple clouds and reflections on the sea; the camera flies slowly, and a short line is written on screen.
entries.fit: The emotional peak, one line such as "Isn't right now the best time?"

entries.name: Eastern Poetic Mood
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: Scenes from classical poetry, such as a moonlit night, a river, a pavilion; can be paired with an interactive web page.
entries.fit: Passages about state of mind or culture; also good as opening titles.

entries.name: Claymation Music Video
entries.category: Mood and Atmosphere (most used in the Feeling track)
entries.description: Clay figures move frame by frame, with a strong handmade feel.
entries.fit: Light, fun passages; your own song can also be made into this kind of music video.

entries.name: Word Architecture
entries.description: Text only. Each word has a "structural role": some are beams, some are columns, some are the floor. The earlier words build up, and the final sentence "stands" on what has been built.
entries.fit: The closing key line "Learn, believe in yourself". The most worthwhile section of the whole film.

entries.name: Beat-Synced Lyrics
entries.description: Lyrics jump out word by word, following the vocals and the beat.
entries.fit: Your own song, or a film with a sung section.

entries.name: Breaking the Frame
entries.description: Something inside a poster bursts out of the poster's border.
entries.fit: Turning points like "breaking out of the old idea" or "no longer feeling it has nothing to do with me".

entries.name: One-Element Throughline
entries.category: Structure and Camera (for linking different styles together)
entries.description: One small thing (an orange dot, a white ball) runs through every scene: first it is a switch, then the dot on a letter, then a curve, then a shape, and finally returns for the ending.
entries.fit: The "thread" when mixing styles. For example, a small dot can stand for "announcement" or "idea" and be followed from start to finish.

entries.name: Single Continuous Take
entries.category: Structure and Camera (for linking different styles together)
entries.description: No camera cuts from start to finish; every scene "grows" out of the previous one.
entries.fit: Passages about change, such as "before you had to push it yourself, now you sit in and it goes by itself", one picture turning into another.

entries.name: Dot-to-Universe Zoom
entries.category: Structure and Camera (for linking different styles together)
entries.description: A dot on a black screen slowly expands into a picture, then keeps pulling back until the whole desktop becomes a dot in space, then pushes into another picture.
entries.fit: Passages about scale, about going "from a small tool to a system".

entries.name: Continuous Shape Morph
entries.category: Structure and Camera (for linking different styles together)
entries.description: The same shape keeps changing: button, loading ring, player, slider, switch... and every change is triggered by a real mouse click.
entries.fit: Passages listing many examples in one breath, such as "organizing spreadsheets, writing weekly reports, batch-editing files, running a content channel".

entries.name: Logo Assembly Intro and Outro
entries.category: Structure and Camera (for linking different styles together)
entries.description: Fragments slowly gather and assemble into the logo.
entries.fit: The opening or closing titles of every episode; make it once and reuse it.

entries.name: Apple Keynote Style
entries.description: Soft, white, bright blue, glass material; the camera never cuts on a still picture.
entries.fit: Passages showing a tool or an interface.

entries.name: Minimal Beat Cuts
entries.description: One shot says one thing, lots of negative space, only one accent color, and every cut lands on a downbeat.
entries.fit: Fast-paced passages, such as "the spreadsheets you organize every day, the weekly reports you write every week...".

entries.name: Fast Vertical POV
entries.description: Vertical format, very fast and fragmented, first-person view, full of action and sound effects.
entries.fit: The first 3 seconds of a vertical version, to grab people.

entries.name: News Flash Roundup
entries.description: Like a news program, going through items one by one, pointing out the highlight of each.
entries.fit: Future roundups like "what's new in AI this week".

entries.description: A brick astronaut builds a rocket out of parts and flies to a brick moon.
entries.fit: Building piece by piece, "build your own system"

entries.name: Paper Pop-up Book
entries.description: A pop-up book opens on a desk, and the little sprite Pip adventures through the paper world and finally jumps out of the book.
entries.fit: Telling a story by turning pages

entries.name: Tilt-Shift Miniature
entries.description: Rush hour in a toy town, where everything looks like a scale model.
entries.fit: Lilliput, looking down on daily life

entries.name: Low-poly Isometric Island
entries.description: Little islands and villages grow tile by tile in an empty sea, a note sounds with every piece placed, until the starry sky.

entries.name: Glass Product Render
entries.description: Unboxing and close-ups of the fictional glass headphones Aura.

entries.name: Line Art
entries.fit: one line drawn all the way through

entries.name: Shape Morph
entries.fit: one shape turning in succession into 6–8 meaningful icons, for example coffee cup→sun→sunset over the sea→seagull→paper plane→location pin→heart; read together with M38

entries.name: Variety Captions
entries.fit: variety-show decorative captions in 9:16 vertical format; a useful reference for captions in vertical versions

entries.name: Hand-drawn
entries.description: Warm empty paper, a thin ink horizon, and an 8-bit mascot that acts out the story, cut against dark title cards and arcade screens.

entries.name: Brand motion graphics
entries.description: A clean explainer that looks like an official brand asset: one dark field, thin white hand-drawn line art, bold type with a single accent, scribbled emphasis, and a persuasion arc from pain to call to action. Silent.

entries.name: Sand art
entries.description: Scenes poured in dark sand on a glowing light table, lit by sunbursts and night skies, that break into grains and blow away between eras. Music and sound effects. Suits stories told through time.
entries.fit: memories, emotions; great for feelings explainers

entries.name: Lyric music video
entries.description: An educational music video that reads like a technical explainer set to a song: a dark grid, a section label in the corner, one diagram per lyric line, and the sung line at the bottom. The engine makes the instrumental; the lyrics are on screen, not sung.

entries.name: Beat-synced footage
entries.description: A high-end, minimal promo cut to a song: a hook that lands word by word on a light stage, the product UI, then real clips on a dark stage as a scanned wall, a 3D carousel, and a phone next to a campaign panel, with stats on push cuts and every cut on a beat.

entries.name: UI morph
entries.description: One interface element that never cuts: a button becomes a loader, a player, a slider, tabs, a chart, a command palette, a toast, and finally the button again, so the video loops. A cursor clicks and drags to cause every change, on the beat. Reference frames are in `docs/styles/uimorph.jpg`.

entries.name: Hero comic
entries.description: A superhero comic book come to life: newsprint pages, thick ink panels, Ben-Day halftone, yellow narration boxes, speech balloons, burst lettering, and a red title slab over flipping pages.

entries.name: Scrapbook
entries.description: A making-of journal on a kraft desk: lined notebook pages, polaroids held by washi tape, torn paper labels, die-cut stickers, rubber stamps, and marker doodles.

entries.name: Torn-paper collage
entries.description: Pictures built from torn scraps of watercolour-tinted paper, laid one by one on a sheet of cold-press paper: skies and seas in long strips, rocks and crowds in small shards, a sun as a torn disc. Calm, handmade, and warm.

entries.name: Particles
entries.description: Thousands of glowing particles drift on a flow field, gather into words, logos, and numbers, then scatter and re-form. The purest "drawn in code" look.

entries.name: Split-flap board
entries.description: A railway departures board: tiles clatter through the alphabet onto each message, amber lamps blink, and a station clock ticks.
entries.fit: airport-style split-flap displays; good for titles and numbers

entries.name: Neon sign
entries.description: Glass tubes on a dark brick wall that buzz and flicker on, glow onto the wall, and reflect on a wet floor.

entries.name: 16-bit arcade
entries.description: A 16-bit console game come to life: a starry violet night, pixel sprites, CRT scanlines, and game UI that turns the story into a run from INSERT COIN to GAME CLEAR.

entries.name: CRT terminal
entries.description: A green phosphor terminal on an old CRT: commands type themselves out, logs scroll, progress bars fill, and big block-letter banners glow for the name and the numbers.

entries.name: Thermal receipt
entries.description: A thermal receipt printer on a teal desk: every scene prints a fresh slip that rises out of the printer, gets stamped, and is torn off. Works in 16:9 and 9:16.

entries.name: Transit map
entries.description: A transit map and station signage: coloured lines are drawn across cream paper, stations light up one by one, a train runs the line, and the ending is the terminus sign.
entries.fit: telling how you got here along the way; suits segment 04 of a multi-segment video (the fourth section)

entries.name: Blueprint
entries.description: A cyanotype engineering drawing: white linework on blueprint blue, dimension lines, numbered balloons, and a title block, as if the product were being specified on a drafting table.

entries.name: Comic book issue
entries.description: A video that stages its content as a physical vintage comic book being read on camera: a portrait-oriented comic page/spread sits centered in the landscape frame against a near-black vignette background, and a virtual camera pans and pushes into individual panels the way a motion-comic or Ken Burns documentary reveals a print page. The book opens with a magazine-style cover, then turns through several two-page spreads of a 2x2 panel grid, and closes on a colophon-style back cover. Panels are built from flat pop-art color blocks (red, gold/orange, blue), Ben-Day halftone dot textures, and sunburst ray backgrounds, with comic sound-effect bursts and a speech-bubble mascot giving it an energetic, Silver-Age-superhero-comic / 1960s advertising-comic feel. The mood is upbeat, punchy, and declarative, reinforced by a continuously driving instrumental music bed with frequent hard transient hits.

entries.name: Documentary
entries.description: A piece that reads like a serious investigative-documentary case file rather than a marketing reel: a near-black canvas holding a slowly turning low-poly "network sphere" emblem, chaptered like folder tabs ("Chapter 1 — ...", "Chapter 2 — ..."), with aged paper "evidence cards" laid under a desk lamp, minimal data-journalism bar charts, and one dramatized "witness testimony" segment shot as a backlit, explicitly-labeled graphic silhouette. Everything moves slowly and settles rather than snaps; captions build up phrase by phrase like narration being typed out; a hushed, low ambient bed with a slow recurring pluck tone underscores the whole thing, broken only by a hard opening hit and a bright closing chime. The net effect is hushed, credible, forensic — closer to a true-crime/60-Minutes case-file open than a tech-hype trailer.

entries.name: Museum exhibit
entries.description: A piece that plays like a nighttime museum special-exhibit walkthrough: a single visitor moves room to room through a pitch-dark gallery where each "diorama" is picked out by one hanging spotlight, a low-poly artifact on a pedestal, a cream museum wall-label, and a docent's caption bar typing out commentary along the bottom. The overall feeling is hushed, reverent, and slightly theatrical — closer to an after-hours exhibit tour than a tech product demo, with warm sepia light carving objects out of near-total black.
entries.fit: laying things out one by one and explaining them

entries.name: Breaking news
entries.description: This clip resembles a cable-news "breaking news" graphics package — the kind of template a 24-hour news channel uses to announce a major story. It opens on a slowly-revealed rotating-globe title card, sweeps a diagonal tri-color ribbon across the screen for the headline stinger, cuts to a flat-vector illustrated news anchor at a desk with a persistent lower-third and scrolling ticker, pushes into a zooming world map (globe → country → city → geolocation pin), then alternates between data/stat cards and the anchor before closing on a minimal logo card. The feeling is urgent, corporate-broadcast, and info-dense: deep navy blues, hard red accents, bold condensed numerals, and a constant on-screen HUD (live clock, channel bug, ticker) that never disappears, evoking authority and immediacy rather than warmth.

entries.name: Detective board
entries.description: This clip reads like a detective's evidence corkboard being filmed and slowly revealed: a warm, lamp-lit cork bulletin board covered in pinned index cards and handwritten sticky notes, centered on a "mugshot" placeholder card for an unidentified suspect. Instead of cutting between shots, a single camera pans and tracks sideways across the board as new evidence cards appear one by one, each strung to the suspect card with taut red thread, building toward a wide "conspiracy board" pull-back. A camera-flash whiteout is the only hard cut in the video, swapping the mystery card for a clean "identified" result card stamped closed. The pacing feels like a true-crime documentary graphics package: steady ticking/pulsing music under a slow reveal, a stab of sharp hits, one big swell exactly on the flash-cut, then a fade to quiet.

entries.name: Picture storybook
entries.description: The video looks like a physical children's picture book filmed lying flat on a wooden desk: a leather-bound cover with gold ornamental corners opens like a real book, then the camera holds a flat, head-on view of each cream-paper spread as it "reads itself" — a circular illustration on the left breathing with small looping motion, and serif body copy typing itself in on the right. The mood is warm, nostalgic, and gentle: soft pastel scene-paintings inside a locket-shaped frame, muted earth-tone data callouts, and a plush round mascot that waves through every scene. It reads as a bedtime-story explainer: cozy rather than corporate, tactile rather than flat-UI.

entries.name: RPG quest
entries.description: A clip that reads like a cutscene lifted from a 16-bit console RPG (SNES/Game Boy Advance era): a fixed-camera pixel-art diorama, a JRPG dialogue box with typewriter text, a "quest log" stat panel, a sword-and-slime battle vignette, a radial-burst level-up screen, and a loot-pickup card, bookended by a night title card and a sunset "quest clear" card. A thin scanline texture sits over every frame, and a chiptune-style pulsing melody drives the pacing. The overall feeling is nostalgic, toy-like, and gamified — factual/data content (benchmark scores, price changes) is translated one-to-one into RPG game-feel (quest completion bars, "+EXP" pickups, loot cards, stat increases).
entries.fit: making learning feel like doing quests

entries.name: Weather forecast
entries.description: A short data video styled as a Korean TV nightly-weather-report broadcast graphics package repurposed for a status update. It opens with a satellite/radar-style storm-spiral animation, then cuts through a sequence of "forecast card" scenes — a temperature-style map, thermometers, wind/speed gauges, a multi-day forecast strip, and a sunny sign-off — each dressed with real broadcast chrome: a channel logo pill, a live date badge, and a scrolling breaking-news ticker along the bottom. The screen stays locked-off and flat; all motion lives inside the graphics (falling snow, twinkling stars, drifting wind lines, a fast diagonal wipe between scenes). A bright, plucky instrumental loop runs under it with an accented musical hit landing on every scene change, giving the whole thing a polished, on-air, slightly playful newsroom feel.
entries.fit: using weather to talk about emotions; great for feelings explainers

entries.name: Home-shopping infomercial
entries.description: The video reads as a parody of a Korean late-night TV home-shopping / infomercial broadcast: a flat, rounded-vector cartoon world where each beat of the pitch gets its own full-bleed, single-hue "sunburst" backdrop, a chunky comic-shout headline slams onto the screen, and a persistent lower-third news-ticker bar keeps scrolling bullet claims underneath. A simple blob-shaped mascot character stands in for "the customer," shown gloomy and gray before the pitch and pumped-up and colorful after it. There is no camera movement at all — it behaves like a slide deck of hard graphic cards, each card populated with big bold numbers, price tags, comparison panels, and cartoon icons (a ticking bomb, a ringing phone, a rocket, a green checkmark). The audio is a bright, dense, evenly-pulsing music-and-SFX bed that stays "hot" almost the entire runtime, occasionally spiking with comedic riser/whoosh effects timed to the hard cuts, giving the whole thing a caffeinated, game-show-auction energy.
entries.fit: satirizing people who sell courses; worth trying for segment 06 of a multi-segment video (the sixth section)

entries.name: Sports broadcast
entries.description: The clip reads like a cable-TV live-sports broadcast package — a night-match stadium open with floodlights and an LED-dot crowd, cut with the on-screen graphics package a network overlays during a match (score bug, "LIVE" badge, lower-third source ticker) — repurposed to walk through a head-to-head stat comparison instead of a game. Motion is entirely 2D broadcast-graphics motion (nothing pans or dollies; text counts up, bars fill, cards slide and glow) cut into short hard-cut chapters every few seconds. The audio is a rhythmic, plucked/percussive pulse that tightens and loosens with the on-screen drama — quieter during the analytical stat-sheet beat, swelling into a bright, confetti-timed climax at the finale — which together with the broadcast chrome gives it the feel of a TV "match highlights" reel rather than a slide deck.

entries.name: Assembly manual
entries.description: The video reads like a printed IKEA-style product-assembly instruction booklet that has been turned into a motion explainer: flat vector line art on aged cream paper, a giant chapter numeral opening every page, an isometric shipping-box "hero" object, a small stick-figure mascot for scale, and literal hardware metaphors (price tags, coin stacks, a conveyor belt, wall outlets) standing in for abstract data instead of ordinary charts. Pages slide over one another like leaves of a manual being turned rather than cutting, each diagram builds itself piece by piece before its number snaps in, and a steady rhythmic tick-track under occasional synth swells gives the whole thing a calm, deliberate, "assembled and verified" feeling that ends on a stamped checkmark held in a still frame.

entries.name: Whiteboard lecture
entries.description: A static "desk-cam" shot of a physical whiteboard, framed by its own aluminum bezel, on which a hand entering from the bottom-right corner writes, draws, underlines, circles, and erases with dry-erase markers and a block eraser — the classic hand-drawn whiteboard-explainer look. Everything is built stroke-by-stroke in real time rather than fading in, numbers get crossed out and replaced live, and nothing is ever fully wiped clean: every earlier section keeps ghosting through as a barely-visible watermark under the current one, giving the board a used, palimpsest-like texture. The mood is brisk, corporate-friendly, and a little playful (circled step numbers, a green checkmark shield, a red circled callout), riding a continuous, steady percussive beat underneath.

entries.name: Movie trailer
entries.description: A prestige announcement trailer that reads like a luxury-watch or car-launch teaser borrowed for a tech reveal: an ultra-wide cinematic letterbox holds a near-black, warm vignette sky sprinkled with slow-drifting dust motes, and every idea — a question, then a date, then a run of benchmark numbers, then the product name, then a release date — gets its own held, centered, fully-faded screen. Nothing cuts hard; everything breathes in as a soft bloom of light, holds, and dissolves through black into the next. The mood is confident and expensive rather than energetic: hushed opening, a rhythmic pulse of swelling hits under the numbers, one big flare-and-impact at the name reveal, then a slow decrescendo fade-out.
entries.fit: next-episode teasers, channel trailers; worth trying for segment 11 of a multi-segment video

entries.name: Math proof lecture
entries.description: A dark, quiet, textbook-like explainer that stages an argument the way a math lecture stages a proof: a title card, a numbered "lemma" per claim, and a closing "therefore" statement with a QED mark. Everything sits on a near-black panel with a faint off-center glow, rendered as flat 2D vector graphics — thin-stroke bar and scatter charts, color-coded equations that build term by term, and small dim citation text in the corner. The mood is restrained and confident rather than flashy: no camera movement, no particle effects, just clean typography and numbers arriving in a steady, metronomic rhythm under a soft ambient pulse.
entries.fit: deriving a conclusion step by step

entries.name: Cinematic Neon Rain
entries.description: One-point perspective of a narrow street on a rainy night, both sides hung with vertical signs, cyan fog thickening with distance, a mass of warm light at the far end of the street; reflections on the wet ground take up half the picture.

entries.name: 80s-90s Retro Anime
entries.description: Cel-painted people and cars speed along an elevated highway at night, tall buildings seen from below, taillights trailing two bands of light; the whole film looks like it is playing from an old videotape.

entries.name: American Comic Street Graffiti
entries.description: Yellow ground, magenta and cyan lightning splits the picture; halftone dots, spray paint, speed lines bursting outward; a person with thick black outlines throws a punch out of the picture, with one big onomatopoeic word beside them.

entries.name: Apocalyptic Industrial Sci-Fi
entries.description: Almost nothing but green; huge mechanical structures stack layer upon layer into the fog, a giant ring in the distance, shafts of light leaking from above; on a walkway, a tiny figure in red wearing a backpack stands with their back to the camera.

entries.name: Pixel Cyber Retro Game
entries.description: Looking down on a street packed with signs, a footbridge crossing it, a big "Sleepless City" screen at the far end of the street, people with umbrellas, small cars, flying cars, and pixel rain falling.

entries.name: Eastern Cyber Fantasy
entries.description: Paper-colored sky, one huge red sun, a line of cranes flying past; by the water, a five-story pavilion with flying eaves, hung with vertical neon signs reading "不夜城" (sleepless city) and "酒家" (tavern) and a screen, its spire ringed by a cyan holographic halo; behind it, pale-ink futuristic towers and mountains, strings of small red lanterns hanging from power cables; on the water, a small boat and a figure in a conical bamboo hat, reflections dissolving like ink wash.

entries.name: Flat Illustration Dusk Rooftop
entries.description: A big gradient dusk sky, three layers of flat-fill city silhouettes, big "NIGHT CITY" neon letters on the rooftop, a person and a cat sitting at the edge of the building, a light-rail train passing behind.

entries.name: Wings
entries.description: a WWI dogfight built in three.js and graded like a 1927 orthochromatic print: whitened sky, very deep blacks, an overall amber tint, gate weave and scratches. *Wings* is famous for aerial combat shot with cameras strapped to the planes, so most camera positions here are mounted on aircraft.
entries.fit: silent-era 3D air combat · orthochromatic black-and-white + amber tint

entries.name: The Broadway Melody
entries.description: a moving black, gold and silver Art Deco musical poster: airbrush gradients, a stepped proscenium, chrome condenser microphones. Broadway in 1929 was at the peak of Art Deco, and this was the film that brought sound pictures, so sound waves ring outward from the microphone.
entries.fit: black, gold and silver Art Deco musical poster

entries.name: All Quiet on the Western Front
entries.description: a Kollwitz-style woodcut: large masses of black, white contours cut with a knife, rough wood grain, with Clawd overprinted from a separate orange block. Kollwitz's anti-war prints of 1921-22 come from the same war and the same grief as this film.

entries.name: Cimarron
entries.description: a 1889 gold-toned albumen print panorama: soft focus, a slight horizontal smear, cream highlights and warm brown shadows, silver-salt grain, with only Clawd hand-tinted. The film opens with the 1889 Oklahoma land run at full gallop, so it is shot with the look of photographs from that year, and this chapter also stays monochrome.

entries.name: Grand Hotel
entries.description: a circular lobby built in three.js, graded in MGM's silver black-and-white, with Clawd's orange as the only color. The film is best known for the shot looking straight down from above, the balconies closing in ring after ring, and the whole set is built around that one shot.

entries.name: Cavalcade
entries.description: a Mucha-style Art Nouveau decorative painting: swollen brown contour lines, pastel flats, a mosaic ground, and a halo behind the central figure. The film opens on a family raising glasses to the new century on New Year's Eve 1899, so the halo is made into a clock face striking midnight.

entries.name: It Happened One Night
entries.description: a 1934 black-and-white rubber-hose cartoon: thick-and-thin ink lines, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, with cel-style flat fills over grayscale watercolor backgrounds and film grain. It dates from the same year as the film, and the gags of a road comedy suit the rhythm of cartoons.

entries.name: Mutiny on the Bounty
entries.description: an 18th-century British Admiralty sea chart in copperplate engraving: rhumb lines, compass roses, depth soundings, hand-applied light washes, with the Bounty as a ship illustration on the chart. The film is about a voyage, so the whole piece stays on the chart.

entries.name: The Great Ziegfeld
entries.description: a rotating spiral "wedding cake" stage built in three.js, in MGM silver black-and-white: satin, chiffon and ostrich feathers set against deep black, with Clawd the only color. The 175-step spiral stage of *A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody* is this film's signature scene.

entries.name: The Life of Emile Zola
entries.description: newspaper letterpress printing combined with 1890s line-engraved illustrations: wood-type headlines, densely set metal-type body text, ink spread and dropout on yellowed newsprint, and figures drawn in hatching. The film's most famous image is the front page of *L'Aurore* on 13 January 1898 with "J'Accuse...!".

entries.name: You Can't Take It with You
entries.description: a 1930s WPA silkscreen poster: six opaque flat inks, split-fountain gradients, slight misregistration, printed on rag paper. The Federal Art Project posters of 1936-39 are the American graphic language of this film's own era, and also set it apart from the newspaper look of Part 10.

entries.name: Gone with the Wind
entries.description: impasto oil painting: palette-knife color blocks, ridges of piled paint, the heat of Technicolor - skies burning from gold to blood red, red earth, black silhouettes. Full color arrives with *Gone with the Wind*, and its first fully colored image is Tara at sunset.

entries.name: Rebecca
entries.description: charcoal on rough-grained paper: velvet blacks, smudged greys, with moonlight and fog erased out with an eraser. Hitchcock's *Rebecca* is a black-and-white Gothic dream, the estate first in fog and then in fire, and charcoal can draw both.

entries.name: How Green Was My Valley
entries.description: opaque gouache in the gold-and-green palette of the 1941 original poster: solid color blocks, coal-black slag heaps, heavy dark Kyffin Williams-style mountain masses and broken outlines. Gouache rather than woodcut sets it apart from Part 3; what it paints is miners singing as they walk down the valley toward home.

entries.name: Mrs. Miniver
entries.description: a stone-lithograph poster of the British home front in WWII: a limited set of brick red, deep green, cream and grey-blue, with shadows in lithographic crayon grain. It matches the film's ending: a village choir singing in a country church with its roof blown open, as Spitfires fly over the hole.

entries.name: Casablanca
entries.description: the look of the film itself: Arthur Edeson's studio black-and-white, painted as retouched stills: soft-focus close-ups with eye lights, venetian-blind shadows, shafts of light in smoke. Clawd, playing Rick, is the only color.

entries.name: Going My Way
entries.description: backlit Gothic stained glass: colored glass held together by lead cames, faces drawn in grisaille, Chartres-blue and ruby borders, colored light spilling across the church floor. Father O'Malley and the choir are set into the window, golden star medallions overhead.

entries.name: The Lost Weekend
entries.description: the picture is typed: monospaced characters on a pica grid, grayscale from character density and overstrike, uneven ribbon ink. Don carries his typewriter to the pawnshop, so the whole street is typed out by a typewriter; Clawd is typed in an orange ribbon.

entries.name: The Best Years of Our Lives
entries.description: a 1946 picture-magazine photojournalism spread: coarse black halftone dots on coated paper, a vertical gutter fold, overprinted captions. Stripped B-17s stretch to the horizon in deep focus; Clawd is printed alone on a spot-orange plate and is the only color.

entries.name: Gentleman's Agreement
entries.description: graphite pencil in the style of 1940s magazine illustration: construction lines laid in first, then pass after pass of parallel hatching, smudged shadows, lifted highlights with an eraser. The picture is drawn up around a polite refusal at a hotel front desk, and only Clawd is in colored pencil.

entries.name: Hamlet
entries.description: a real-time 3D Elsinore in high-contrast deep-focus black-and-white: volumetric fog, wet stone, waves breaking into lacy white foam, silver-halide grain. Shot after the castle, the fog-bound battlements and the rocks in Olivier's film; Clawd is the only color.

entries.name: All the King's Men
entries.description: a Southern campaign poster in wood-type letterpress: red, blue and black inks on buff paper, solid areas showing wood grain, uneven inking, plate misregistration, portraits in halftone dots. This is Stark's campaign rally, with Clawd printed in a fourth plate of orange ink.

entries.name: All About Eve
entries.description: Al Hirschfeld's Broadway caricature: flowing ink lines of varying thickness, solid black blocks, abundant white space, each person caught by a single exaggerated feature. The film is about the theater, so the party is drawn as a newspaper theater-page caricature; Clawd is the only color.

entries.name: An American in Paris
entries.description: Raoul Dufy's watercolor: quick blue-black ink lines over transparent patches of cobalt blue, lemon yellow and rose pink, the line and the color never lining up. The film's closing ballet set was designed after Dufy's paintings, and the Place de la Concorde and the dancers are drawn his way.

entries.name: The Greatest Show on Earth
entries.description: Strobridge circus chromolithograph: flat chrome yellow, vermilion and cobalt blue with heavy black outlines, halftone dots, misregistration and stone grain. DeMille's big top is painted as a three-ring poster, with Clawd as Sebastian doing the trapeze catch.

entries.name: From Here to Eternity
entries.description: 1953 high-key black-and-white: hard sunlight, darkened sky, whitened surf, wet sand reflecting the sky, silver-halide grain and halation. Shoot the kiss in the waves of Halona Cove; Clawd, sitting on the lava rock blowing a bugle, is the only color.

entries.name: On the Waterfront
entries.description: Ben Shahn's social realism: trembling offset ink lines over offset flat tempera color blocks, workers with big hands and long faces, color held to gray-blue, brick red and ochre. Shahn painted dockworkers and the union, exactly the world of this film.

entries.name: Marty
entries.description: a 1955 television recording, playing on a TV in a warm Bronx living room: scanlines, phosphor glow, a rounded convex screen, snow, with only Clawd in color. The original was a live television play, so it is shot as television.

entries.name: Around the World in 80 Days
entries.description: 1950s flat geometric cartoon: color blocks and ink lines printed out of register, broken ink lines, crayon grain on cream paper. The film's six-minute end-title animation is by Saul Bass, in exactly this modernist manner.

entries.name: The Bridge on the River Kwai
entries.description: a general arrangement drawing pinned to a drafting table: white lines on Prussian blue, fold creases, water stains and red-pencil revisions. The film is about a colonel determined to get his bridge built properly, so the bridge is drawn as his engineering drawing.

entries.name: Gigi
entries.description: Toulouse-Lautrec-style chromolithograph: large flat areas, dry-brush contours, spattered ink dots in place of halftone, caricature-like faces. Gigi's moment is walking into Maxim's with all of Paris turning to stare at her, exactly the Paris Lautrec painted.

entries.name: Ben-Hur
entries.description: a procedurally generated 3D grand arena with the epic light of widescreen: desert midday sun, dust, marble and gold, Technicolor grading and 65mm grain. The chariot race is the film's most famous sequence, so it shoots the race directly, with the poster's golden colossus overhead.

entries.name: The Apartment
entries.description: Saul Bass-style white lines slide in over black to build the film's most famous one-point-perspective endless office hall, then fill in with gray tones. Bass made this film's title sequence; the only warm color in the whole frame is Clawd and the key tag.
entries.fit: Saul Bass line title sequence · black-and-white

entries.name: West Side Story
entries.description: a 3D Upper West Side block under a red-orange Technicolor sunset, saturated and theatrical: red brick, zigzag fire escapes, rooftop water towers, dancer figures that can strike poses. It restages the film's overhead opening, the Jets snapping their fingers and the leap on the poster.

entries.name: Lawrence of Arabia
entries.description: epic-poster gouache with visible brush direction and strong warm-cool contrast: an amber desert against a cobalt-blue sky. The original *Lawrence of Arabia* poster was painted by Howard Terpning in exactly this manner.

entries.name: Tom Jones
entries.description: a Georgian satirical print: Hogarth-style engraved lines of varying thickness and directional hatching, brushed over with Rowlandson-style bright hand-coloring that spills slightly outside the lines, plus one speech bubble. The film itself imitates the 18th-century England that Hogarth drew.

entries.name: My Fair Lady
entries.description: quick dry-brush ink lines with pink and magenta watercolor washes and flicked spatters, dissolving into the white paper at the edges. The 1964 original poster was Bob Peak's ink line with pastel color; the scene is Ascot in black and white, designed by Cecil Beaton.

entries.name: The Sound of Music
entries.description: a storybook-feel procedural 3D Alps: saturated emerald, cobalt and snow white, sculptural ridgelines, cotton-ball cumulus clouds, waves of wind through the grass. It restages the opening helicopter shot, ending on Maria twirling on the mountaintop.

entries.name: A Man for All Seasons
entries.description: an old-master oil portrait: smooth glazed modeling, fur collars painted hair by hair, velvet highlights, gold chains rendered link by link, plus aged varnish and craquelure. Holbein himself painted Thomas More in 1527, and this uses his composition.

entries.name: In the Heat of the Night
entries.description: three-color Risograph printing: deep blue, poster orange-red and fluorescent pink, with halftone dots, grain and misregistration; light is printed by laying down less ink. It echoes the orange-red heat-wave ground and black silhouette of the 1967 poster.

entries.name: Oliver!
entries.description: a Victorian toy paper theatre: hand-colored lithographed cardboard figures with scissor-cut white edges, layered scenery slotted onto sliding rods, candle footlights beneath a gilded proscenium casting shadows on the scenery. *Oliver!* is a musical and fits a Victorian family's small stage perfectly.

entries.name: Midnight Cowboy
entries.description: Warhol's photo silkscreen: a black halftone photograph layer printed unevenly, pressed out of register over loose flat color blocks on a silver ground, the image repeated two and three times. The film has a Warhol-Factory-style party, and his Elvis was exactly a cowboy.

entries.name: Patton
entries.description: a lithograph look imitating 1940s US war bond posters: graded flat folds, dark contours, halftone shadows, yellowed paper. It matches the opening of *Patton*: the small general addressing the troops before a giant flag filling the stage.

entries.name: The French Connection
entries.description: the whole Brooklyn street under the elevated railway built in 3D, then graded to coarse-grained 16mm: cold gray, teal-leaning shadows, high contrast, gate weave. The film is best known for the car chase under the elevated tracks, and only 3D can capture that speed.

entries.name: The Godfather
entries.description: oil painting in deep amber and umber, warm only where the overhead light falls: shadows are thin transparent glazes, lit edges are impasto. It recreates the overhead light of Gordon Willis in that study where "I believe in America" is spoken.

entries.name: The Sting
entries.description: magazine illustration in the line of Leyendecker and Rockwell: lit planes, parallel brushstrokes, crisp dark contours. The film's chapter cards imitate *Saturday Evening Post* covers, and the 1936 betting parlor is drawn the same way.

entries.name: The Godfather Part II
entries.description: a turn-of-the-century toned silver-gelatin photograph, hand-colored: sepia toning, soft focus, silver grain, mold spots, torn corners, with faint touches of red, blue and verdigris. It depicts young Vito arriving at Ellis Island in 1901, like a Lewis Hine photograph.

entries.name: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
entries.description: a quiet realism in the manner of Edward Hopper: large flat pale green walls, hard-edged parallelograms of low morning light, people kept apart from one another. This suits the ward in *One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest*: order under fluorescent light, broken by one escape.

entries.name: Rocky
entries.description: early-morning Philadelphia built entirely in 3D, from the meat locker to the 72 steps of the museum, graded as 1970s 35mm: cold blue sky, a low golden sun, long shadows, thin haze, fine grain. Running up the steps and the circling rise at the top are this film's signature moments.

entries.name: Annie Hall
entries.description: A New Yorker single-panel cartoon: lively pen-and-ink lines, a few restrained light washes, lots of white paper, and a hand-lettered caption line underneath. Woody Allen's comedy and this magazine share one tone, and the lobster scene is practically a gag cartoon already.
entries.fit: New Yorker single-panel cartoon · ink line and light wash

entries.name: The Deer Hunter
entries.description: Egg tempera in the manner of Andrew Wyeth: dry, fine cross-hatched short strokes in low-saturation straw yellow, ochre brown and grey green, every blade of grass drawn individually, a pale sky. Wyeth was a Pennsylvania painter, and the one-shot deer hunt takes place in the mountains above a Pennsylvania steel town.

entries.name: Kramer vs. Kramer
entries.description: A kitchen drawn in a child's crayon: wobbly lines, color pressed hard into the paper grain and out past the outlines, labels and arrows, a sun with a smiling face. This is how Billy sees making French toast with his dad.

entries.name: Ordinary People
entries.description: Layered transparent watercolor: wet-in-wet sky and lake, edge lines left by water pooling, backruns, bare paper as highlights, autumn gold and rust red set against cool grey-blue. It suits the quiet, slightly sad Lake Forest autumn that opens the film.

entries.name: Chariots of Fire
entries.description: A four-color lithograph in the manner of the Jean Droit poster for the 1924 Paris Olympics: classical figures, limited inks, clumped lithographic grain, uneven registration. Chariots of Fire is about the 1924 Olympics, and the beach run looks like that poster come to life.

entries.name: Gandhi
entries.description: Hand block-printed cotton: indigo, madder red and turmeric yellow with black carved-block outlines, colors misregistered at the block seams, dye bleeding along the warp and weft. Hand-spun khadi is Gandhi's emblem, so the Salt March is printed as a length of cloth.

entries.name: Terms of Endearment
entries.description: A family photo album lying open, filled with faded Polaroids and Kodak snapshots: greenish blacks, cream highlights, white borders. One of the Polaroids comes alive as a panning shot of a beach car chase. Terms of Endearment spans thirty years of mother and daughter.

entries.name: Amadeus
entries.description: Black paper silhouette portraits edged in gold, filling horseshoe-shaped gilded boxes and red velvet, facing a stage with a starry-sky backdrop. The high point of Amadeus is opening night, one picture holding the orchestra pit, stage, audience and Salieri in the shadows.
entries.fit: Rococo silhouettes · candlelit golden opera house

entries.name: Out of Africa
entries.description: Low-altitude real-time 3D flight: a chrome-yellow biplane skims a soda lake, tens of thousands of flamingos startle into the air, amber misty light. The most remembered moment of the film is Denys flying Karen over Kenya, and the hand she reaches back to the rear seat.
entries.fit: 3D biplane over the East African Rift

entries.name: Platoon
entries.description: Fast, forceful pen lines with light washes in olive green, dusty yellow, smoke grey and flame orange, with sketchbook paper left white at the edges. It looks like something a combat artist drew on the spot, close to the film's infantryman's-eye view of Vietnam.
entries.fit: Vietnam combat sketch · pen and light wash

entries.name: The Last Emperor
entries.description: Iron-wire-line drawing on silk with layer upon layer of azurite, malachite, cinnabar and gold paint, ruled-line architectural palaces, thousands of kneeling court officials. The boy emperor's enthronement is a Qing court ceremony, so it is painted the way Qing court painters recorded ceremonies.
entries.fit: gongbi heavy-color painting · court painting on silk

entries.name: Rain Man
entries.description: Smooth airbrush gradients, hard-edged masks, chrome highlights and pink-green neon, with a layer of fine cyan counting annotations on top. 1980s art style meets the world through Raymond's eyes: 82, 82, 82, 246 toothpicks in all, and card counting at the table.

entries.name: Driving Miss Daisy
entries.description: Solid, warm Rockwell realism: clean edges, visible brushwork, afternoon sun through oak trees, neighbors each busy with their own thing. The film is just two people in a car in 1950s Atlanta, already like a Saturday Evening Post cover.

entries.name: Dances with Wolves
entries.description: A soldier's field journal: pencil lines that vary in weight, transparent watercolor, yellowed rag paper, handwriting in ink and pencil notes in the margins. Dunbar keeps a writing-and-drawing diary throughout the film, so the prairie comes alive out of his sketches.

entries.name: The Silence of the Lambs
entries.description: Fine copperplate hatching and stippling with a thin layer of hand coloring on top, plate numbers and Latin labels printed on yellowed paper. The death's-head hawkmoth on the poster belongs on a specimen plate, and the same cold copperplate treatment carries on into Lecter's cell.

entries.name: Unforgiven
entries.description: Impasto Western oil painting in two tones: a plain under Remington's gold-red sunset, and his late blue-green night scenes lit by warm yellow window light. Unforgiven opens and closes on a silhouette at a grave under the setting sun, and the showdown takes place in a small town on a rainy night.
entries.fit: Remington Western oil painting · sunset and rainy night

entries.name: Schindler's List
entries.description: Cold grey, high-contrast black and white, coarse grain, blooming highlights; only the little girl's red coat and Clawd's orange carry color. This is exactly Spielberg's device: the red coat and the Sabbath candle flames are the only color in the whole film.
entries.fit: black-and-white film · the single red coat

entries.name: Forrest Gump
entries.description: Printed cards folded upright along parallel creases, white paper core, grey board edges, drop shadows between layers and shallow depth of field, set on a walnut desk. Forrest sits on a bench and tells his whole life as a story; turn a page and a stretch of his life stands up.
entries.fit: pop-up book · paper craft on a real desk

entries.name: Braveheart
entries.description: A page from a medieval manuscript: burnished gold leaf with punched dots, lapis-lazuli blue, vermilion, blackletter script, with a window-like battle miniature in the middle. Braveheart is a Scottish legend, and the final cry of FREEDOM at the end is made into a gilded initial.

entries.name: The English Patient
entries.description: Watercolor sketches pasted into an old book, tucked with maps, photographs, notes and pressed flowers, the whole thing in the poster's amber brown. Almasy's Herodotus stuffed with drawings and notes is the frame of the whole film, and the camera passes through one watercolor into the Cave of Swimmers.

entries.name: Titanic
entries.description: White lines on Prussian-blue blueprint paper rise up and grow perspective, then develop into a full-color 3D ship at sunset, running on into the night. The ship itself is the film's emblem, so the shipyard drawings and the live scene use the same model.

entries.name: Shakespeare in Love
entries.description: Elizabethan court miniatures in the manner of Nicholas Hilliard: opaque watercolor on parchment, an ultramarine ground, shell-gold lettering, white wild roses. The film is set in Shakespeare's London, and the miniature was exactly the portrait form of that court.

entries.name: American Beauty
entries.description: Two kinds of picture cut together: first a clean, saturated, frontal and symmetrical suburban house (red door, red roses), then a cut to low-resolution DV footage with a REC interface. It matches Lester's respectable suburbs in the film and the plastic bag footage Ricky shoots.
entries.fit: symmetrical suburban cinema frame + DV footage

entries.name: Gladiator
entries.description: The whole picture is laid in square stone tesserae and glass pieces: the stones along the outlines follow the form, flat areas are laid in straight rows, and the gold-leaf glass pieces glint. The film itself is set in Rome, so the Colosseum and the Elysian wheat field are both made as Roman floor mosaics.

entries.name: A Beautiful Mind
entries.description: Handwritten math on two surfaces: white grease pencil on the glass of a Gothic library window and chalk on a blackboard, with the numbers lighting up and joined by gold lines. This is how Nash sees patterns in the film: it is light in his head, not a computer interface.
entries.fit: formulas on a window and chalk on a blackboard + golden connecting lines

entries.name: Chicago
entries.description: A black stage cut by hard-edged spotlights: six cells holding female prisoners in red-rimmed silhouette, a neon C behind them, sequins and smoke, Clawd in a white follow spot. This is the film version of "Cell Block Tango", in the poster's red and black.

entries.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
entries.description: Soft watercolor and pencil landscapes with deep atmospheric perspective, plus an ink-line map on parchment. The film's concept art was painted by Alan Lee and John Howe, so the journey is told the way the trilogy was first drawn.

entries.name: Million Dollar Baby
entries.description: An original 16-bit arcade fighting game screen: health bars, a round timer, ROUND 1 / FIGHT!, a combo counter, hit-stop and a giant K.O. A boxing championship movie becomes one round fought in arcade grammar.

entries.name: Crash
entries.description: A retouched night photograph drawn in code: white and red headlight trails on an overpass, sodium-lamp orange against neon cyan, reflections on a wet road, out-of-focus bokeh, and snow that is only visible in the light. The ending of Crash is a rare snowfall in Los Angeles.
entries.fit: Los Angeles night light trails + falling snow

entries.name: The Departed
entries.description: Flat multi-layer spray-paint stencils with overspray fuzz and drips, paint sinking into the brick joints, a torn wheat-pasted poster beside it. The last shot of The Departed is a rat crawling along the railing beneath the golden dome of the State House, and street stencil graffiti has always loved painting rats.

entries.name: No Country for Old Men
entries.description: A real-time 3D West Texas wasteland at dusk: the sun pressing on the horizon, long shadows pointing at the camera, low-saturation dusty yellow and grey-green, fine grain. It follows the light Deakins shot for the Coen brothers, and the poster's man carrying a case in backlight.
entries.fit: 3D West Texas wasteland at dusk (Deakins light)

entries.name: Slumdog Millionaire
entries.description: A blue-violet TV studio with gold highlights, moving-head light beams and lens flares; then a cut to saturated orange-and-teal Mumbai rooftops. The film itself cuts back and forth between the final question of the quiz show and the slum where Jamal grew up.
entries.fit: quiz show studio + Mumbai orange and teal

entries.name: The Hurt Locker
entries.description: A page from a US Army bomb disposal manual: even black lines, hatched shadows, stippled sand and soil, circled numbers and leader lines, an exploded IED diagram, with just a touch of olive green and sand. The Hurt Locker is about procedure under pressure, and the manual diagram is that procedure drawn out.
entries.fit: bomb disposal field manual line drawing

entries.name: The King's Speech
entries.description: An interior with a heavily textured wall, in the feel of oil paint: the cool grey-green, many-layered peeling wall of Logue's consulting room, then the amber-gold padded broadcast room with its spring-suspended microphone and thin golden sound waves. It follows the walls Eve Stewart designed and the poster's golden yellow.

entries.name: The Artist
entries.description: Clean, luminous black and white: bright highlights, soft grey scale, Art Deco bordered title cards, slight flicker and grain; Clawd is the only color. The Artist is a 2011 love letter to silent-era Hollywood, so it is more polished than O1 (Wings).

entries.name: Argo
entries.description: A 1970s Kirby comic spread open on a production desk: heavy ink lines, Kirby energy bubbles, four-color dots on yellowed newsprint. The fake sci-fi film in the story used exactly Kirby's concept art, so the comic turns its pages from the fake epic all the way to the real runway escape.

entries.name: 12 Years a Slave
entries.description: A 1850s daguerreotype in a brass-framed velvet case, developing from blank: a violin leaning on a chair, Clawd standing beside it with head bowed. This is photography from Solomon Northup's era, using a single object to tell the whole film, with no person drawn.

entries.name: Birdman
entries.description: A detailed 3D Broadway theater backstage, shot as a handheld long take: warm tungsten lights against cold fluorescents, ending in the glare of Times Square. Birdman is best known for pretending to be a single take, so the style of this piece is that camera move.

entries.name: Spotlight
entries.description: A picture printed in newspaper halftone dots, placed on the grey-green screen of a microfilm reader: scanlines, a rolling scan band, dust on the glass. The reporters in the film dig up the truth in exactly this kind of archive, and the cuts are made as microfilm lateral slides.

entries.name: Moonlight
entries.description: Oil portraits in saturated teal, magenta and moonlight blue, sculpted heads repainted with brushstrokes that follow the form. Painted straight from the line in the film's title: "In moonlight, black boys look blue."

entries.name: The Shape of Water
entries.description: A flooded bathroom and laboratory tank in real-time 3D, the whole picture soaked in teal: flowing caustics, shafts of light falling from above, bubbles and a few warm lamps. Del Toro's film is steeped in this kind of water, so the whole sequence is shot underwater.

entries.name: Green Book
entries.description: A "Greetings from the South" linen-texture postcard come to life: cloth-grain paper, saturated airbrush color, star-shaped glints on the chrome. The film is a 1962 road trip through the American South, on exactly the kind of roads shown on these postcards.

entries.name: Parasite
entries.description: An architectural section cut through a Seoul hillside: a glass mansion on top, a secret bunker underground, and a route running all the way down to the flooded semi-basement, in fine lines and soft material colors. Parasite is built on exactly this vertical class divide, and one drawing holds the whole film.

entries.name: Nomadland
entries.description: Powdery pastel strokes on grey-violet paper, a wide plain and an old camper van, the sky shifting from golden yellow to rose to violet. Nomadland lives on that long, empty horizon at dusk, and pastel makes it quiet and soft.

entries.name: CODA
entries.description: A polished sperm whale tooth on an oak table, engraved with fine black lines and touches of red, blue and yellow: Gloucester fishing boats, a family hauling in nets, Ruby singing at the bow. It is the folk craft of the New England coast where the film is set.

entries.name: Everything Everywhere All at Once
entries.description: Four universes, four looks, all real-time ray marching: the cold green IRS office, a hot dog finger piano under commercial lighting, a silent canyon with googly-eyed stones, an everything bagel turned black hole. As in the film, the jumps between universes are made with a googly-eye sticker.

entries.name: Oppenheimer
entries.description: A real-time 3D reconstruction of the Trinity test site before dawn: a fireball of about 720,000 particles, a quantum vision made of orbits and waves, deep blue night against orange-gold firelight, with IMAX-style grain. Oppenheimer is built around this single flash of light.

entries.name: Anora
entries.description: Pink, teal and orange neon tubes glowing, their reflections dragging across a wet boardwalk and falling into drifting snow, with bloom, out-of-focus bokeh and grain. Anora runs from the Russian neon of Brighton Beach to the wedding signs of Vegas, all lit by tube light.

entries.name: One Battle After Another
entries.description: A real-time 3D desert highway that rises and falls like a roller coaster, three cars chasing each other over ridge after ridge, shot with an extreme telephoto, with heat haze, bleached glare and fine grain. It recreates the film's most famous sequence: the rolling-highway car chase.
